[[Category:Launcher (Primary)]] {{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|The Ogris fires detonite infused casings.}} The '''Ogris''' is a {{Faction|Grineer}} rocket launcher that fires {{D|Blast}} rockets that explode over a small area, but can also [[stagger]] the player if they aren't careful. A [[AT Ogris|slower projectile version]] of this is used by the [[Bombard]], though the homing ability isn't present on the version used by the Tenno. It can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Chem Lab|Chem Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals {{D|Blast}} damage. *Rockets explode in a '''7.1''' meter radius upon impact with a surface or enemy. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. **Enemies can destroy the rockets with gunfire or area of effect explosions. *Can be fired while sprinting. *Can use the Ogris-exclusive {{M|Nightwatch Napalm}} mod, and the launcher-exclusive {{M|Adhesive Blast}} mods. *Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. {{Advantages|class=Launcher| *Very fast charge speed. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Launcher| *Projectiles have travel time. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 20% from central impact. }} {{WeaponComparison|Kuva Ogris}} **Trigger type (Charge vs Semi) ==Acquisition== The Ogris's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Chem Lab|Chem Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *Both the actual rocket and the explosion can deal critical hits. *The 100 damage of the rocket is dealt upon impact, and can therefore normally only hit one target. *Charge can be held indefinitely, allowing the user to prepare a shot before it is needed, or hold a shot while changing positioning. **[[One-Handed Action]]s will not cancel the charge, including all [[One-Handed Abilities|one-handed abilities]] and most maneuvers. Notable exceptions are rolling and making a hard landing. **Interacting with consoles will not cancel charge unless you are required to hack them. **Pressing reload while charging will cancel the charge. If the magazine is not full, it will also reload the weapon. This is also true for {{Weapon|Lanka}}, {{Weapon|Ballistica}}, {{Weapon|Opticor}} and {{Weapon|Drakgoon}}. *The Ogris's 100 base accuracy makes it difficult to see any additional rockets generated by [[Multishot]]. ==Trivia== *The Ogris received a visual remodel in {{ver|16}}, giving it a bulbous appearance in line with other Grineer weapons. **Its new appearance shares several visible parts with the {{Weapon|Torid}}, implying that the Torid is an Ogris with [[Infested]] parts. **Prior to {{ver|16}}, it used a simpler, box-shaped model. ***The old Ogris model humorously had "{{GrineerScript|BIG HURT F43}}" - Grineer for "BIG HURT F43" - written on both sides. This is odd considering it is a clan-made version and not a direct copy of the ones used by the Grineer. **Prior to {{ver|8.1.3}}, the only indicator of the charge-up time was the noise, which was often difficult to hear in the middle of firefights. ***The exhaust tubes and clip now vibrate and wobble when charging and when fully charged. **Prior to {{ver|9.5}}, the Ogris used the same reloading animation as most other rifles, which resulted in the player appearing to empty a non-existing magazine and slapping the bottom of the weapon. **The old model returned in {{ver|38.5.11}} in the [[Galleon of Ghouls]] [[Tactical Alert]] in the form of a self-damage weapon in the mission and the [[Volatile Ogris Skin]] reward. *The Ogris' magazine is a drum that is loaded on top of the weapon. This drum spins when the Ogris is fired. *{{ver|18.4.10}} removed one of the biggest issues with the Ogris, the "jam" experienced when not fully charging a shot. The Ogris would be unable to begin charging another shot after partially charging and cancelling for any reason. *Uses the same lighting effect as shooting an explosive barrel. *Decreasing the charge time of the Ogris using fire rate mods will increase the pitch of the charging sound. *Prior to {{ver|13}}, rockets from the Ogris were unable to pass through Volt's {{A|Electric Shield}}, instead they would collide with the shield and explode. *Prior to {{ver|19.10}}, rockets stuck to enemies with {{M|Adhesive Blast}} would cause damage over time, with a chance to proc status effects, including {{D|Slash}} to lethal effect. *The Ogris' slight charge-up before firing is similar to the [[Wikipedia:RPG-7|RPG-7]] rocket launcher. *Starting December 10th, 2020, this weapon, along with the {{Weapon|Drakgoon}} and {{Weapon|Stahlta}}, had a themed skin which could be obtained for free from the Epic Games [[Unreal Tournament Weapon Bundle]], formerly available on the Epic Games Launcher. **On December 9th, 2024, the skins were made available upon login until December 23rd, 2024, after which the skins were permanently added to the [[Market]] for {{cc|1}}. ==Bugs== *Firing at [[Lephantis]] does not deal explosive damage to the targeted area (only the damage of the projectile impact is counted). ==Media== Ogris 1.png|Ogris as it appears in the arsenal Ogris 02.png OgrisCodex.png|The Ogris in the Codex as of Update 16. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 5 Ammo per Pick Up: *Ogris ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. ;OPTIMIZATIONS: *Optimized the particle FX on the Ogris. {{ver|30.8}} *Fixed some overlapping textures on the Ogris Unreal Rocket Launcher Skin. {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Ogris: 80% {{ver|27.2.1}} *Decreased the distance to point of impact that Self Stagger is inflicted with the Shedu due to having a large AoE range. {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. {{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Creates and focuses a high-frequency field of microwaves, literally cooking the target from within.}} The '''Nukor''' is a {{Faction|Grineer}} sidearm that fires a microwave-like frequency beam that inflicts {{D|Radiation}} damage, boasting an extreme [[critical multiplier]] is heavily offset by its almost nonexistent [[critical chance]]. It also has a unique status effect called {{D|Microwave}} that enlarges enemy body parts. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals {{D|Radiation}} damage. *Can inflict a unique status effect called {{D|Microwave}}, enlarging the body part that was shot at. *Damage ramps up from 30% to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 30% over 2 seconds. {{Advantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held| *Second highest [[critical multiplier]] of all weapons in the game, behind {{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}}. *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. **{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. *Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held| *Limited range of 25 meters. *Pulsing weapon effect blocks the reticle, making it harder to make consistent headshots with the weapon shooting at moving targets. }} {{WeaponComparison|Kuva Nukor}} **Lower range (25m vs 29m) ==Acquisition== The Nukor's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Chem Lab|Chem Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== *Nukor can proc an invisible [[Status Effect]] called {{D|Microwave}} that causes the part of the enemy hit to become larger. **Microwave procs have infinite duration, but the visual effect does not. **Microwave counts as an individual status for {{M|Condition Overload}}, {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}}, {{M|Galvanized Savvy}}, and {{M|Galvanized Shot}}. **Some enemies are not affected by this [[Status Effect]], at least visually, for example [[Liches]] ==Tips== *There are several ways to make use of the Nukor's high critical damage by adding flat critical chance bonuses: **An [[Adarza Kavat]] with {{M|Cat's Eye}} can give your weapons an additive 60% boost to critical chance. **Likewise, [[Smeeta Kavat]]'s {{M|Charm}} can guarantee orange crits as one of its possible effects. **Using the [[Secondary Fire]] of the {{Weapon|Mutalist Quanta}} and afterwards firing the Nukor through the orb adds a flat +25% critical chance, in addition to +25% critical damage and extra {{D|Electricity}}. **{{WF|Harrow}}'s {{A|Covenant}} can add up to +50% additive crit chance, or +200% on headshots, after absorbing enough damage. **A fully ranked {{Arcane|Arcane Avenger}} has a 21% chance upon receiving damage to grant +45% flat critical chance. **{{Arcane|Secondary Enervate}} can gradually increase the Nukor's critical chance until a set number of [[Critical Hit#Crit Tiers|tier 2/orange/big]] critical hits. *With a maxed {{M|Primed Target Cracker}} and {{M|Hollow Point}}, the Nukor can achieve a critical damage multiplier of 10.8x, the highest critical damage multiplier value achievable outside of red crits. **It is however ill-advised to use Hollow Point if attempting a critical damage build due to the Nukor's extremely low [[critical chance]]. *The Nukor's short range, high accuracy and cone of fire means that {{M|Magnum Force}} can be used to provide additional damage without severe penalty. *The Nukor can be made into an effective anti-[[Sentient]] weapon by adding {{D|Cold|icon=Cold}} damage which, in combination with its innate {{D|Radiation}} damage, allows the Nukor to deal extra damage against Sentients while freezing them with Cold status effects. ==Trivia== [[File:Grineerheavyhugehead.jpg|thumb|142px|A [[Heavy Gunner]] trapped in {{WF|Vauban}}'s {{A|Bastille}}, with her head expanded by a Nukor.]] *This is the first known manufactured [[Grineer]] energy weapon and the second gun to deal pure radiation damage, the first being the {{Weapon|Detron}}. **The {{Weapon|Seer}} is ''technically'' the first Grineer energy weapon, as its projectiles appear to be energy; as well when reloading the magazine, an energy-like substance appears to discharge. Though there is the possibility that these projectiles could be superheated materials. **The Seer is also composed of Orokin technology, and not actually made by the Grineer entirely; this can bring to question whether or not the Grineer possessed the technology and/or know how to create an energy source or if it was simply salvaged from the Orokin tech. *As a microwave beam weapon, the ''Nukor'' could be considered a [[wikipedia:Maser|maser]] - such devices work similar to lasers, but using lower frequency microwave radiation. **The name itself is likely a nod to 'nuking', a term used to refer to cooking/reheating food or drink using a [[wikipedia:Microwave oven|microwave oven]]. *As the Nukor is being fired, its magazine will rotate and its front encasing will slowly open up. This can be assumed to be a method of cooling the weapon as it heats up during operation.  *The aimed body part of the target inflates in size as the target is damaged, as demonstrated by the picture above, identical to the effect of {{M|Peculiar Growth}}. This also works on bosses and other Warframes in PvP. *Enemies killed by the Nukor dissolve in a fashion similar to {{WF|Nova}}'s {{A|Molecular Prime}}, however this effect is purely visual and corpses can still be {{A|Desecrate}}d. **If said enemies had been killed by Nukor damage and sliced in half, the corpses will reappear. *Oddly, the Nukor has two separate energy colors when used with its default palette, being orange for the weapon energy colors themselves and blue for its radioactive beam and warped circles. **This however changes when the user is applying their own energy color and will apply the single color to both. *Previously, the Nukor's beam was treated as a source of AoE damage (such as an explosion) from point of contact of the Nukor's beam, allowing it to penetrate [[Shield Lancer]]'s shields (not to be confused with [[Punch Through]]). ==Media== NukorCodex.png|Nukor in Codex. The '''Ocucor''' is a {{Faction|Corpus}} beam pistol incorporating {{Faction|Sentient}} technology, releasing energy tendrils on kills that assault the closest target.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Radiation}} damage.
*Damage ramps up from 20% to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 20% over 2 seconds.
*Kills with this weapon releases an energy tendril that can home-in on enemies close to the targeting reticle, up to a maximum of '''4''' tendrils.
**Tendrils lock on to enemies within '''40''' degrees of the reticle. Tendrils will stay locked on until enemies are '''60''' or more degrees away from the reticle.
**Tendrils disappear upon [[reload]]ing or emptying the magazine.
*Can equip the Ocucor-exclusive {{M|Sentient Surge}} mod.

{{Advantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held|
*Pinpoint [[accuracy]].
**{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon.
}}

{{Disadvantages|class=Pistol|trigger=Held|
*Very inefficient ammo economy.
*Limited range of 20 meters for both the main beam and the tendrils.
}}

==Acquisition==
The Ocucor's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] in the [[dojo]].

{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*Tendrils are generated by killing an enemy with direct damage of the primary beam, or through status effects dealing damage (e.g. [[Damage/Heat Damage|Heat]]'s burning effect). Status kills will generate a tendril regardless of if they originated from the primary beam or a tendril. Direct kills with tendrils will '''not''' generate an additional tendril.
*Tendril ''base'' damage is the same as the primary beam. Tendrils can score critical hits and status effects independent of the primary beam.
*Tendrils homing in on the main beam's target are only cosmetic, and don't deal any additional damage or status effects.
*Tendril range is affected by {{M|Ruinous Extension}}.
*Tendrils reset if the reloading process is started or the magazine reaches zero. Even if reloading is cancelled or the weapon is holstered, the tendrils will still vanish.

==Tips==
*Magazine refill effects such as reloading upon [[holster]] (from the [[Set Mods#Synth Mod Set|Synth Mod Set]] or {{M|Eject Magazine}}), {{M|Blood Forge}}, or kills with {{M|Sentient Surge}} or the {{Resource|Ack & Brunt Incarnon Genesis}}'s Rogue Readiness perk will prevent the tendrils from disappearing. Additionally, [[Cyte-09]]'s [[Cyte-09/Abilities|Resupply]] will also prevent loss of tendrils while adding new elemental damage types to shots fired.
**{{M|Sentient Surge}} is almost essential for this weapon, massively increasing its effective critical chance and status chance and letting its tendrils stay active for much longer.
*With all tendrils active, the Ocucor can inflict a massive amount of status effects; Arcanes that rely on triggering a high amount of certain status effects like {{Arcane|Cascadia Flare}}, {{Arcane|Cascadia Empowered}}, and {{Arcane|Secondary Shiver}} work very well with it.
*Tendrils aim for the torso, and as such cannot trigger {{Arcane|Arcane Pistoleer}}. However, it can still be triggered from the main beam, massively increasing the Ocucor's ammo efficiency and time between reloads.

==Trivia==
*The Sentient component of this weapon appears to be a modified [[Shwaak Prism]], particularly with the "arm" that connects the Prism to a given [[Amp]] removed. The energy tendrils themselves however are more similar to the [[Klebrik Scaffold]].
*Though Ocucor is a secondary firearm, there is a ring that looks similar to [[Jai#Jai|Jai]] Link attached to it. This aesthetic is shared with {{Weapon|Battacor}} and {{Weapon|Kreska}}.
**According to [[:File:Lucas-hug-crpsenthybrid1.jpg|Lucas Hug's concept art]] however, the rings are merely [[wikipedia:carabiner|carabiner]]s meant for easy transport. 
*The Ocucor's name, like the Battacor, seems to be a portmanteau, incorporating [[Oculyst]] (a Sentient enemy) and the suffix ''-cor'', seen in some other Corpus weapons.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage.
*Releasing the shot after 70% of a full charge, indicated by white brackets and the reticle turning yellow, will perform a "Perfect Shot", with higher [[critical chance]] and [[critical multiplier]] over a fully Charged Shot.
**Both Charged and Perfect Shots feature a significantly larger projectile and [[Infinite Body Punch Through]].
*Four innate {{Pol|V}} polarities.
*Quick shots have a forced {{D|Impact}} proc.

{{Advantages|class=Bow|
*Infinite ammo.
}}
{{Disadvantages|class=Bow|
*Charged and Perfect Shots have a [[headshot]] multiplier of 1x.}}

==Acquisition==
Nataruk is given upon completion of [[The New War]], complete with a free weapon slot and a pre-installed [[Orokin Catalyst]].

Additional copies of Nataruk can be bought from [[Cephalon Simaris]] for {{sc|100,000}}.

==Notes==
*Charged and perfect shot arrows are coated with Void-like trails and "explode" on impact.
**However, despite the visuals, the weapon has no area of effect properties.
*The projectile hitbox of both the perfect shot and the charged shot is quite large, allowing the player to hit enemies and even achieve headshots without needing to be perfectly precise.
*Arrows do not arc while travelling.
**Arrows also have infinite travel distance, traveling in a straight line until they hit an obstacle or go out of bounds.
*Not [[Noise Level|Silent]], making it ill-suited for stealth. This can be remedied by equipping {{M|Hush}}.
*No [[headshot]] multiplier on charged or perfect shots. Quick shots will still benefit from headshots, however.

==Tips==
*Equipping mods that boost fire rate such as {{M|Speed Trigger}} or {{M|Vile Acceleration}} allows for faster charging and consequently more charged shots fired, but can make it harder to land the timing for a perfect shot.
**{{M|Critical Delay}} can be used over {{M|Point Strike}} to more finely adjust the fire rate to your personal liking and comfort.
**Be also mindful when in a squad with allied Warframes that have base or augmented abilities boosting fire rate (such as {{WF|Wisp}}), and the respective adjustment needed to still land perfect shots.
**Reload Speed modifiers such as {{M|Radiated Reload}}, {{Arcane|Primary Merciless}} and {{A|Speed}} can also directly speed up the time between shots, but without affecting the charge time.
*({{M|Primed Shred|Primed}}) {{M|Shred|Shred}} is an excellent mod that provides both Fire Rate (for faster charged shots) and Punch Through (to ignore small pieces of terrain and corners that shots might otherwise clip).
*The perfect shot's large hitbox and ease in achieving headshots benefits from headshot-focused mods and arcanes such as {{Arcane|Arcane Rage}}, {{Arcane|Primary Deadhead}} and {{Arcane|Longbow Sharpshot}}, as well as Warframe abilities like {{A|Covenant}}.
**When using ({{M|Galvanized Scope|Galvanized}}){{M|Argon Scope}}, you must continue to hold your zoom whilst the projectile is traveling to maintain the bonus. Consider pairing it with {{M|Terminal Velocity}}.
*Due to charged and perfect shot having large and long lasting visual effects, it is recommended to use darker energy colours to reduce screen noise.
*The size and intense glow of the Perfect Shot projectile can make it difficult to control if combined with {{WF|Ivara}}'s {{A|Navigator}}, so if both are going to be used together, darkening the energy color will be beneficial.
*{{WF|Nidus}} can make devastating use of this weapon in conjunction with {{M|Teeming Virulence}}; cluster enough enemies with {{A|Larva}} and use {{A|Virulence}} to trigger the augment's effects, then finish off any surviving targets caught in the mass.

== Known Bugs ==
* Despite listing 0.1s reload time (0.05s rounded up), the reload time is actually 0.6s.
* {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} is multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits from perfect and charged shots.

== Incarnon Form ==

When newly acquired from the [[Foundry]], players must acquire '''100''' kills with the Onos in order to gain access to its Incarnon transformation. Each challenge additionally grants 5,000 [[affinity]] to the weapon, affected by [[Affinity Booster]]s. The following Evolution tiers, their requirements for unlocking them, and their related perks, are shown below.

=== Overview ===
* Incarnon Form is activated by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by achieving [[Enemy Body Parts|weakpoint hits]] and then pressing the [[Alternate Fire]] button. '''12''' weakpoints will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
** Charges do '''not''' generate on the backpacks of most [[MOA]] variants, or vulnerability spots generated by {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}} in places other than actual weakpoints.
** Weakpoints on corpses or [[Invulnerable]] targets do '''not''' build charges.
** Individual [[Multishot]] bullets can build charges.
* Mode switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's [[reload speed]].
** Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.
* Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Onos's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing '''30''' rounds to a maximum of '''350'''. Once all ammunition is expended, the Onos reverts to its normal form.
** Incarnon Form's magazine is '''not''' affected by mods.
** Incarnon Form is '''not''' affected by [[Ammo Efficiency]] (such as the '''Ruptured Plenitude''' or '''Agile Executor''' perks or {{A|Energized Munitions}}).
** Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as [[holster]]ing, [[bleedout]], or being [[disarm]]ed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon [[death]].
*** Onos' Incarnon form cannot be activated while mounted on any [[K-Drive]], including {{A|Merulina}}. Mounting a K-Drive while Onos' Incarnon Form is active will force the Onos to revert back to its default form. Forcing the Onos to revert to its default form in this manner '''<u>will not consume</u>''' any Incarnon charges.

<section begin=intro />
'''Neutralizer''' is {{WF|Cyte-09}}'s [[Exalted Weapon|Exalted]] Sniper Rifle, summoned by activating the ability {{A|Neutralize}}. Primary fire shoots sniper shots that [[ricochet]] on [[Enemy Body Parts|weak points]], while its [[Alternate Fire]] lobs a {{D|Cold}} grenade.<section end=intro />

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Puncture}} damage on its primary fire and pure {{D|Cold}} on its [[Alternate Fire]].
*Shots [[ricochet]] on [[Enemy Body Parts|weak point]] hits up to <u>'''4'''</u> times within {{Stat|Ability Range|icon=only}}'''10''' meters of the target, with a damage loss of <u>'''20%'''</u> per ricochet.
*Three zoom modes:
**First zoom has 2.5x zoom distance and +40% critical damage multiplier.
**Second zoom has 4.0x zoom distance and +60% critical damage multiplier.
**Third zoom has 8.0x zoom distance and +80% critical damage multiplier.
*[[Alternate Fire]] launches a grenade that explodes in a <u>'''10'''</u> meter radius, inflicting <u>'''10'''</u> {{D|Cold}} stacks and leaves a lingering field for <u>'''5'''</u> seconds.
*Can use the sniper-exclusive {{M|Target Acquired}}, {{M|Harkonar Scope}}, and {{M|Sharpshooter}} mods.
*Innate {{Pol|V}} and {{Pol|Bar}} polarities.

{{Advantages|name=Neutralizer|*Innate 2.5 meters [[punch through]].}}

{{Disadvantages|name=Neutralizer|*Requires {{Stat|Ability Efficiency|icon=only}}'''5''' [[energy]] to activate. Primary fire shots consume {{Stat|Ability Efficiency|icon=only}}'''10''' energy, while Alternate Fire consumes {{Stat|Ability Efficiency|icon=only}}'''20''' energy and '''3''' ammo.
*Cryo Grenade projectile has travel time with heavy arcing.}}

==Notes==
*Neutralizer uses [[Rifle Mods]] and can equip [[Sniper Mods]].
*Neutralizer appears in the [[Arsenal]] after unlocking Cyte-09's {{A|Neutralize}} ability.
*Despite the UI indicating otherwise when modding, the alternate fire forces Cold and cannot be altered by elemental mods.

==Tips==
*Synergizes with {{M|Spectral Serration}} and {{M|Primary Acuity}} due to {{A|Evade}} and {{A|Seek}} respectively.
*For conditions requiring status effects afflicted by abilities like [[Arcane Impetus]], the Alt-fire enhanced with an ammo pack behaves like an ability applying a status effect. The guaranteed status effect from ammo packs on the regular shot will not proc those effects however, and will be treated as purely a weapon instead.
*Can hit through the shield of Profit Taker's pylons if {{A|Seek}} is active.
